#3570. 12 Best Video Game Stocking Stuffers Under $30 That People Actually Want

Ugh. It’s my least-favorite time of year: Black Friday season. I hate this overwhelming capitalist-ass shopping holiday for many reasons, but one of my more petty pet peeves is the big push for the blandest, most cringey “gamer”-themed gifts ever at mainstream shopping destinations. I’m talking like, this “Smells like video game rage” candle, neon lights and blankets that say stuff like, “Can’t hear you, I’m gaming,” or the classic “I paused my game to be here” T-shirt. Crap that really leans into the awful “gamer” stereotype and that, for many of us, is embarrassing to receive from a relative who knows, like, one fact about us, which is that we are into video games.

If you’ve arrived at this article and have been guilty of giving such gifts before, please absolve yourself. The internet does not make this easy. Gaming gift guides are full of this junk, and if you’re not into games yourself, finding decent stuff for someone who likes them can be really annoying and challenging, especially on a budget. Most gamers probably have a lot of the tech and games they want already, and knowing what people have and what they might like can be extremely challenging if you don’t have an easy way to look at their Steam libraries.

So I’m here to give you a hand with 12 ideas for stocking stuffer gifts (read: will reasonably fit in a normal-sized Christmas stocking) under $30 that will probably be relevant to folks who like playing video games on the regular. These are all things that most people will be at least mildly pleased to receive and will probably use as long as you put in the bare minimum amount of thought to make sure you’re not getting Switch accessories for someone who doesn’t have a Switch or something.

Good controllers are so dang expensive and cheap ones are usually garbage, but the 8BitDo controllers are both of solid quality and inexpensive. Normally $29.99 on Amazon, as I write this they’re on sale for $22.99.

It’s normally $49.99, but Amazon has a Black Friday deal going that brings it all the way down to $18.99, so you may want to jump on it soon.

However, my experience is that not a lot of people are using this feature, not because it’s a bad idea necessarily, but because they don’t want to buy the expensive bespoke webcam Nintendo is selling and don’t want to move the normal one they have on their PC over to their Switch every time. So right now, for $24.98 on Amazon ($34.99 normally) you can grab a Hori USB camera that’s licensed by Nintendo and works with the Switch 2. Actually having this set up with the Switch 2 will probably prompt more people to actually bust it out (it would certainly work on me).

If your gamer likes to sit at a desk, grab ’em a mug warmer like this Sweetfull option that’s currently $16.99, down from $19.99. It’s exactly what it sounds like, keeping the liquid warm. Great for tea, coffee, and hot cocoa drinkers who have told their families to stop buying them tea/coffee/cocoa every year because they now have too much.

It’s a little cliche, but I don’t know anyone who doesn’t think a light bar is at least a little cool. This one is inexpensive ($11.99 right now, down from $14.99), simple, and looks nice, though it’ll probably stick out of the top of the stocking a bit and give away your game.

Great for PC gamers. Comes in several colors and is $8 max when not on sale. Sounds lame, but is actually very useful. The sort of thing no one buys for themselves but is always grateful to get.

Check first, but an awful lot of people who are into video games pair that interest with a card-collecting hobby. PokÃ©mon cards are a nightmare to get nowadays, but if you can snag a pack or two from the 30th Celebration set, most PokÃ©mon card fans will be happy. Magic: The Gathering‘s Reality Fracture set is a good, safe bet for Magic fans, and the One Piece TCG is currently on a set called The Dominance of God.

Zojirushi is a great brand that makes a lot of great things, including water bottles. These things are durable and can support hot or cold bevvies, and from personal experience I can say it keeps cold water cold for hours. There are aÂ tonÂ of really cool, low-cost stickers, skins, and cases out there with which to protect one’s Nintendo Switch, and chances are your gamer wants one, because unless they have a sick special-edition Switch, those things are very bland aesthetically. Loads of them are under $30 and they come in all sorts of colors and styles. Just make sure you’re confident in which Switch (original or Switch 2) they have, so you get them one that fits.

#3569. Rumoured The Simpsons: Hit & Run remake may be in trouble after one developer says their "mind-blowingly awesome" project is cancelled

A rumored remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run (the internet's most-wanted video game revival) may be in trouble.

Just earlier this year, Radical Entertainment made somewhat of a comeback as New Radical Games - with the original studio's co-founder (Ian Wilkinson) and former developer (Tim Bennison) serving as New Radical's CEO and COO, respectively. The company best known for Prototype and the well-remembered open-world Simpsons game was back, in some sense.

Whatever project the studio was cooking hasn't been so lucky, it seems. New Radical Games senior game designer Darren Evenson recently said an upcoming project at the company had been scrapped, and he's now looking for new work, per a LinkedIn post.

"It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at New Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations," Evenson wrote. "A gaggle, I say!"

"Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets... will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money... and if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power... and... well, there's more to that quote, but I digress."

"For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people," he added. "Please reach out, shout out, or perform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to."

New Radical Games has never formally revealed its plans, but a couple clues pointed to something Simpsons-shaped. As VGC noted, Evenson's statement echoes a few popular lines from the iconic animated sitcom. "Will you ever learn" is suspiciously close to a particular Troy McClure quote, for one.

Then there's seemingly a Scarface riff in the developer's statement - one that was also parodied in The Simpsons, of course: "In America, first you get the sugar, then you get the power, then you get the women." It's worth noting Radical Entertainment did also make Scarface: The World Is Yours, so this one could go either way.

But the most eyebrow-raising clue came from original Simpsons co-showrunner and creator Matt Groening. During a Disney D23 panel this summer, Groening and current showrunner Matt Selman were asked about the possibility of a Hit & Run comeback.

"I don't know [if] I'm speaking out of turn, I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening said at the time, before Selman quickly chimed in: "Or not…"

"Hit & Run is so interesting. I'm a thousand years old, and when I was in my mid to late 20s, I helped write Hit & Run," Selman said back in March. "I had no idea it would become a cult game, a cult success. Of all the games, the thousands of Simpsons games... that one..."

In 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die, suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

In an interview on Alchemy with Anthony Mason, while promoting his new movie Ink, Mason brought up Boyle’s prognostication, and Boyle took it one step further, saying:

But we have an actor in [Ink], Jack O'Connell, [who] would have been a great Bond, as well.  And now I can see that in all this talk, they're talking about Jack O'Connell as a possible villain. They have that thing you want to watch them.  And it's impossible to quantify what it is. Otherwise, we’d all buy it for ourselves.

O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another big casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy, has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

Last week, after the Pattinson announcement, Brad Pitt even tossed his own name into the ring for the role. Now that would be an interesting choice! The latest rumors also point to Tom Hardy as the next villain, which would set up an interesting dynamic between the current Batman (Pattinson) and a former Batman villain (Hardy played Bane in The Dark Knight Rises).

There are still quite a few casting announcements for Bond 26 to look forward to, like M, Q, and Moneypenny, in addition to the villain, maybe a henchman or two, and, of course, the next Bond Girl. Oh, and who could possibly be in line to do the next Bond theme? It’s an exciting time to be a Bond fan. Meanwhile, Ink will be available to watch with a Netflix subscription on January 8th, after a short stint in theaters starting on December 11.

#3567. Yooka-Laylee studio explains upcoming Definitive Edition's absence on Xbox to 'frustrated' fans

"As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face."

Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs."

The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version.

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post.

"We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

Playtonic said it understood Xbox players' frustrations, but the development costs associated with bringing the game to more platforms "just isn't viable for us at this time." Playtonic is still an independent game studio, after all, and Xbox console sales have been lagging behind the competition for quite a while.

"As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback," the statement went on.

Digital Foundry's John Linneman chimed in to tell folks that the omissions isn't a huge deal, because Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair already looks pretty great on Xbox consoles. "The Xbox One X version of this game is already native 4K," he tweeted. "The upgrade seems minor, thus it's already excellent on Xbox. Was the best console version by far."

The original Yooka-Laylee was a collectathon throwback in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie, but this follow-up took more inspiration from Rare's Donkey Kong Country games instead - and the results were pretty stunning.

"It's the new in Impossible Lair which impresses, the tightness of the game's 2D controls and intricately designed levels which stands out, and which seems better fitted to Playtonic's toolbox," Eurogamer's review said. "It's a far more polished game than the studio's predecessor, and one well worth exploring through."

The attention to detail in GTA 6 is astounding, but one particularly impressive facet comes from how Jason and Lucia move when their hands are full. Rockstar Games' director of animation, Mike Jones, says it "took months" to properly animate all of those specific and rare animations.

Whenever Jason and Lucia have a sandwich in one of their hands and a drink in the other, for example, the devs needed to change the way the characters interact with the wider world. How do they whip out their phones, or hug each other, or open doors? If Lucia's holding a sports bag full of dirty cash while shooting police with a normally two-handed shotgun, how might she reload her weapon?.

"We put a huge effort into the details, which means teams caring about something as mundane as how the players might use a door when carrying drinks. Lucia may turn her back to open a door with her hip whilst her hands are occupied. That took months of development, but it matters," Jones says in quotes given to GamesRadar+ ahead of our GTA 6 review.

In a follow-up post on BlueSky, Jones reveals that the developers actually "made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left."

The process was apparently "a massive pain but once you knew every interaction could 'cope' it made the game logic much easier." Some of those animations were then "sometimes replicated" whenever Jason and Lucia are crouching, too.

The arduous development process was well worth it, though. GTA 6 is both the highest-rated game of all time - if review aggregation website Metacritic is any indication - and the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

After 4 hours in Blackrock Depths, I'm not sure anymore.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

Dungeons in MMOs have gone through quite an evolution—in ye olden days of Everquest (and WoW Classic, more on that in a second) they were multi-hour sprawling crawls that were sometimes even designed to be done in multiple play sessions.

Nowadays, if you have a dungeon that takes more than 30 minutes, folks start getting the itch—and honestly, it's fair enough. Not everyone has the kind of free time for MMOs anymore, and the daunting prospect of pushing in half a 9-5 workday just to get a max-level dungeon run cleaned up is not appealing to anyone with other responsibilities in their lives.

However, as someone who recently did an all-bosses (plus the Jailbreak escort) Blackrock Depths run, which took four goddamn hours of my actual life, I'm not sure on which side of the fence I sit anymore. Ask me a couple of months ago, and I'd say that maybe an hour is pushing it.

But I cannot help the fact that I had an absolutely wonderful time with my fellow dungeon-divers—strangers, all, and yet I felt a certain camaraderie with them, even for the hunter who kept hanging way too far back in the Lycean and pulling extra groups.

I am not a tank, and yet I tanked—and over the course of those four hours turned from apologising profusely for forgetting my Demoralizing Shouts to a field marshal that ordered the whole group into the corner so we wouldn't wipe on the last room.

When we looped back for the Jailbreak quest, me and the three other people still left (our fifth understandably had to go) were yelling at Marshal Windsor, who kept turning and opening doors, ordering us to work through a list of his own petty grudges when we'd already been there for the length of a Lord of the Rings film. We went a little mad.

And there's something sad about the idea that this kind of experience—a sprawling, labyrinthine crawl done in one sitting because everyone involved is too stubborn to come back later—isn't really a thing in modern MMORPGs anymore.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Not only did it endear me to a bunch of group mates I would've otherwise never talked to, it also made me grow attached to BRD as a location. What would have simply been a non-memorable three-boss rinse with a narrow path in a more modern MMO was a real adventure.

What do you think? Am I just nostalgic? Are these types of dungeons deservedly banished to the pit in 2026? Or should MMOs waste our time again? Here's a poll to find out. Also a comments section below, if you'd like.

The Lycean can go do one, though. That room is awful.

#3564. 12 Astonishing Indie Games To Buy Or Wishlist This Thanksgiving Day

It’s Thanksgiving! The annual pause from the incessant thankstaking that otherwise consumes us all, and as is traditional all around the world, we remember the day Earth was recaptured from the Xix Muthra Horde through the celebration of indie gaming. In a ceremony that goes as far back as 2022, we’ve picked out a pile of lesser-known indie games that we can stuff on our Steam wishlists with mad abandon.

Whoever named this “Thanksgaming,” however, has a lot to answer for. It doesn’t even work as a pun, let alone communicate that this is a collection of unknown indie games submitted to Kotaku by email, and then somewhat randomly selected and featured on the site. It’s all about offering you an eclectic range of fabulous-looking games that you can add to your wishlist, or buy and play right now, that you’d otherwise not likely see on a major gaming website. So dive in! If nothing here takes your interest, then your interest is poorly calibrated. You should get that checked.

Developer: SoÃ­n, Talbone Release Date: TBA Steam, Itch

Drifting meets rhythm gaming in this space-based taxi sim. That was a fun sentence to type out, because I don’t think there’s any other job in which you’d get to do it. It’s about racing around the solar system to underground Brazilian DJ beats, all with the goal of paying an “infinite debt.” And, well, watch the trailer! It’s amazing! Look at that astonishing art, and listen to what I’m going to pretend I already knew was Baile Funk. There’s a demo on Steam.

Developer: Victor Vergara, Alex Vergara Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

While an obvious nod to Geometry Wars,Â Geometry Rift appears to be a lot more than an homage to Bizarre Creations’ bizarre creation. This bullet hell roguelite blends the arcade classic withÂ Vampire Survivors elements, to create a full-frontal assault on your eyes. The nice kind, though. I mean, it looks beautiful, and I very much want to be playing it. Which I can, via the demo on Steam! This is being created by a father and son team from Spain, and was nominated for inclusion here by a third-party who just wants to see it getting more attention.

Developer: Lunheim Studios Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

At long bloody last someone’s finally combined pachinko and dungeon crawling. I was beginning to get annoyed.Â Peglin opened the door, andÂ Bumpers and Dragons has stepped through it. It’sÂ PeggleÂ as violence, where your bumpers are weapons, bought, upgraded and arranged on the board as you see fit, in a roguelite with a procedurally created set of dungeons and permanent progression.

Developer: Longhand Electric Release Date: Out now Steam

I loves me any game that lets me step inside paintings, whether it’sÂ Mario or this intriguing-looking free game.Â The Stone Ship came out in July, but completely passed me by (I’m installing it as I type). It’s a first-person game where paintings, photographs and maps come to life as you shift into their depicted scenes, scored by a gorgeous violin soundtrack composed and performed by Caroline Karpinska. ApparentlyÂ The Stone Ship was originally intended to be a chapter from a 2025 game,Â Overlook Trail (which also looks amazing!), but grew into its own standalone entity.

Developer: Jeffrey Nordin Release Date: Out now Steam

Released a couple of weeks ago, but yet to get attention, is the stunningly-namedÂ The House Dreams Along With Them, a first-person puzzle game in which you bring dreams into reality while exploring a modern-looking home. It’s about discovering the “reification of night,” which is a phrase that has brought me a great deal of pleasure. Inspired byÂ Myst (pwt-ooey),Â The Room and escape rooms, it looks splendidly bizarre. There’s a demo on Steam.

Developer: AstronautCat Studios Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

This trailer properly spooked me! It’s superbly well put together, compiled from the found footage of a missing cinema employee.Â Late Shift is about exploring and spotting anomalies in a looping reality that evokes Backrooms-like creepypastas, but showing clear and welcome influences from Control as well. Its mix of art styles, impossible architecture and jumpy nature feel really evocative to me. Can’t wait.

Developer: TMA Games Release Date: Out now (Early Access) Steam

Torment Hexus had me at “kicking CEOs out of windows.” It also had me at combining match-3 spellcasting alongside a tactical roguelite combat grid. What I’m communicating is that it has me. Now, at least: this entered Early Access in August this year, and intends to emerge fully-formed by some point in 2027. It’s currently playable, “pretty smooth and polished,” they say, but there are plans to add many more bosses, new spells, and a big ol’ story to justify multiple runs through the intriguing concept.

Developer: Mullet Games Release Date: 2027 Steam

Building a city in the desert is hard enough, what with the lack of water and basic resources, but what about the massive sandstorms blowing in and burying your settlement in sand? That’s the setup forÂ Storm Settlers (a name I struggle to see how Ubisoft will allow, given the genre overlap with itsÂ Settlers franchise), a super-cute and challenging city-builder. To survive your little guys will have to dig down in the hope of discovering the water table, while also building up defenses against the ceaseless storms that sweep over your town. The game is having a public playtest in December.

Developer: Pixelnest Studio Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

One of my favorite phenomenon is watching as rudimentary gaming genres cross over and develop complexity, as if driven by the same forces that cause evolution to keep pointing things toward becoming crabs.Â Cosmo Cargo is a great example of this, merging the trend for inventory management games with the trend for auto-battlers, and creating a space-exploration game with hireable crews, hostile enemies, and battles based on the synergies created by the way you’ve combined cargo in your inventory. There’s a demo, of course, and the game is out next year.

Developer: ElSchorscho Release Date: December 2 Steam

I have a real soft spot for the dumbest incremental games, with their moreish progression and self-effacing inherent nonsense, and Drunk Woodcutter perfectly fits that bill. Due out next week, the short game is about chopping logs with increasingly silly tools…while getting drunk. This leads to hacking at logs with a banjo, and making money in the process, and as such reflects all our lives.

Developer: Lost Token Release Date: Out now Steam

Theropods is a traditional point-and-click adventure, but with the twist of containing no words or dialog at all. You play as a young cave women living with a tribe, haunted by dreams of the gruesome death of her mother in the mouth of a dinosaur. Yup, it’s a dinos and cavemen living together story! TakeÂ that, evolution. Now an adult, she needs to get on with the caveperson life, be it hunting, mending pots, or saving her people from the terrifying attack of marauding enemies, raging fires, and alien artifacts falling from the sky. Doing this with no words at all makes for a simpler game, but an intriguing one, boosted by some utterly stunning old-school pixel art animations.

Developer: Speldosa Interactive Release Date: Dec 7 Steam

A third-person platformer crossed withÂ PowerWash?! Yes please! That’sÂ Muri: Wildwoods where you play as an adorable mousey cleaning up and restoring an island to make it all lovely. To get around, it’s third-person jumping and climbing, and there are even watergun-based puzzles to solve. Powerwashing with double-jump is something I didn’t know I needed, but now it’s all-consuming. Thankfully there’s only a couple of weeks to wait until it’s out!

#3563. After drawing ire for selling new Mass Effect merch following BioWare closure, EA is now flogging new Dragon Age tat too

Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.

EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, quickly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, new Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time (thanks IGN) to promote a new "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

"Unless you reopen BioWare, EA, then no money for you," one person wrote in a social media response indicative of the general sentiment from others. Some users also used the opportunity to share the #savemasseffect hashtag beneath the BioWare Gear post - a related community initiative has so far seen over 330,000 fans sign a petition to save the series.

The community has been energised by glimpses of what could have been following Mass Effect 5's cancellation. At one point, a flashy internal trailer appeared online, and award-winning composer Austin Wintory also shared music he'd pitched for the game. Elsewhere, content creators claiming to have seen a work-in-progress version of Mass Effect 5 have called it "incredible" and claimed it would have drawn lessons from The Witcher and Baldur's Gate 3.

BioWare's closure in October came as part of the first round of layoffs at EA since the publisher's $55bn acquisition by a consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, investment firm Silver Lake, and private equity company Affinity Partners earlier this year. The move resulted in the loss of 400 jobs, with layoffs occurring across multiple studios, including Apex Legends developer Respawn, The Sims studio Maxis, and EA Motive.

It's wild to think about but Survivor has been on the air for 26 years now. The competition series (which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) started its run back in 2000, and longtime fans are still up to date with the current Season 51. A lot has changed over the years, including Survivor's prize money, the amount of days the game lasts, and how casting works. I recently watched a vintage clip from back in Season 2, and it totally made me miss OG Jeff Probst.

The second season of the show was titled Australian Outback, and is arguably one of the best Survivor seasons in the show's long history. Some of the most iconic players ever came out of Season 2, including Jerri Manthey and the great Colby Donaldson. I recently saw a clip of a wildly dangerous challenge, and I was shook by how different the entire show feels nowadays. You can check out the video for yourself below:

A post shared by Susie Mac (@survivordeepdive)

Honestly, how crazy is this Survivor challenge? Rather than the standard ones we're used to seeing every season, the above clip shows Jeff asking the cast to jump off a cliff and try to survive floating down rapids with boxes of supplies. It's truly terrifying to watch it play out, especially when you consider that Rodger Bingham had only JUST learned to swim before starting the game.

I loved re-watching this unique challenge, as I've grown tired of seeing the same ones every single season. I mean, how many times can we watch the contestants do the same puzzle? The show's early seasons used to have challenges that were themed based on their location, making each one unique. Although as we know, Survivor has been permanently based in Fiji since Season 33. So the location-based theming has been gone since 2016.

Seeing this retro Survivor clip also made me miss the OG version of host Jeff Probst. While he's pretty warm and cuddly nowadays, he used to be more of a hard ass. I used to love hearing him throw shade at the contestants, often adding salt to fresh wounds in the process. Seriously, he used to call people or tribes "completely useless" back in the day. This always cracked me up, but nowadays the host/showrunner is more likely to give folks a warm hug.

Jeff used to be scary during classic Survivor, but that's simply not the vibe anymore. I mean, castaways are so comfortable around him they're willing to interrupt his speeches and even give him a nickname like "Uncle Jeff." Where's the respect, people?

Survivor airs new episodes Wednesdays as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if Probst ends up changing his tune at all throughout the rest of Season 51.

#3561. GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

You cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

Much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

Yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

But as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

So on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

But even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time issue, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a big plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. But given all the crime I’ve been doing, somehow I feel that a happy and normal future will, like the many, many restaurants of Leonida, be forever closed to them.

#3560. Digital Extremes says Warframe's imminent Tau update is practically big enough to be a sequel as it reveals new details, including dog walking

Warframe's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new update, which arrives on 9th December. Additions include a two-hour long quest, new explorable areas, and even chill nighttime dog walking.

In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford said. "It is a second solar system ... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a new solar system brick-by-brick."

That begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a new navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The Perita is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

Then there's the ringed city of Fornax. Unlike previous regions in Warframe, this features three hubs: the Lastbloom Lounge, Manifold 90-BF, and the Elder Rustgarden. All have their own playable missions, some brand-new and others returning from the original star system. This includes Spy, a returning mode that has players breaking into terminals while trying to remain undetected.

Spy hasn't been shown a lot of love for a while, and it seems like this new iteration will bring new custom puzzles for players to take on. Ford notes it'll include codes to memorise, passwords to figure out, plus gameplay and an aesthetic that alights with the new Fornax setting.

Steel Path - the optional, more difficult variant of regular missions - also returns in Tau, although the Accolite mini-bosses who would hunt you down in previous Steel Path missions will not be present. Instead, the Hokra brothers will take that role: giant sentient casino goons who look quite daunting.

We were also shown more of the Last Bloom Lounge. Here you'll be given bounties that'll always bounce you between the three Fornax hubs. So, if you take one bounty in the Lounge, you'll complete it while out on a mission, and end up in either Manifold or the Rustgarden (which is still being kept secret for now). That way you'll be naturally circling between the three locations.

However, rather than there being three separate syndicate reputations to grind out, one single syndicate connects them all: the Fornax Informer, a newspaper run by kids obsessed with breaking stories across the ringed city. Print lives! By progressing through the ranks with this syndicate, you'll unlock clues for detective work that reveal a special cinematic within the Lounge, though this too is being kept secret for now.

By completing bounties, you'll also gain access to Fornax's own progression system which provides still-mysterious buffs and other beneficial effects within Tau. There's also a card game in the Lounge, which you can either play against the house or with other players.

As for navigating between the hubs, each one has its own garage. The Tau update comes with a driving minigame: an on-rails opportunity to gather resources and fend off other drivers along the way. In the demo shown, we're brought from the Lounge to the Manifold, dodging barriers and blowing up other sentient vehicles in the process. There's also a "low stakes, no combat" way to navigate between the hubs. It's called Night Walk, a first-person dog walking mode where you can travel

This Gigabyte Gaming A16 laptop at Best Buy is down to $1,235, and when I saw those specs with that price tag, I felt a (brief, fleeting, but much-needed) sense of relief. Now there is a decent laptop at a reasonable price. So they do exist.

Gigabyte's Gaming A16 has a bunch of things worth mentioning, but the best part is certainly the Nvidia RTX 5070 GPU. That's a midrange GPU at what is now an almost budget-level price, so it's genuinely a good deal. The caveat here is that it's the 85 W version, so it's not the most powerful iteration of the RTX 5070 you'll ever get to see, but at this price? I'll take it.

Apart from the RTX 5070, which, with the help of DLSS 5, should be able to carry most games at reasonable settings, you're also getting the AMD Ryzen 7 260 laptop CPU, a 1 TB SSD, and 16 GB DDR5 RAM. Display-wise, we're looking at a 1920 x 1200 resolution with a 165 Hz refresh rate. All in all, very respectable.

Shopping now, during the Cyber Monday sales, gives you $365 off the regular list price. That's a whole lot of laptop for under $1,300, so I'd jump on this deal while it's still up.

5. Best high-performance: Lenovo Legion Pro 7i Gen 10

As Christmas inches closer, fans are getting more into the spirit thanks to the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Hallmark once again offers a large variety of classics and has over two dozen new holiday films this year. A massive number of people have already been watching Countdown to Christmas. However, the network’s beloved lineup does not just include the main channel. Hallmark’s Christmas classics have also made their way to Hallmark+. I love the holiday films, and there are two great ones that you can only watch on streaming, for the most part, that is.

Get in on this Black Friday deal through Amazon to save big on your first three months and watch all the best Christmas and other holiday movies the streamer has to offer. Including movies that are only available on Hallmark+.

Now that Thanksgiving is over, fans are looking forward to the holiday season. And to get into the Christmas spirit, if you haven’t already, Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas is just the thing. Of course, while the network has been showing Christmas movies 24/7 for several weeks now, Hallmark+ has even more to watch. And that means even more movies that actors have had to film during the summer. For Black Friday, fans can sign up for just $2.99 for the first three months (perfect for those upcoming cold winter nights). That includes many Hallmark series and movies, as well as exclusive originals only available on Hallmark+. After those three months, it's either $8.99 per month or $79.99 per year, and it includes plenty of great offers.

As previously mentioned, there are a handful of originals exclusively for Hallmark+, such as the When Calls the Heart prequel Hope Valley: 1874, which is coming back for Season 2. This includes the four-movie Unwrapping Christmas collection that premiered back in November 2024. Even though they premiered two years ago, the movies definitely still hold up, and two of them are arguably the best in the series.

Unwrapping Christmas follows four friends working at a gift-wrapping shop leading up to the town’s Christmas gala. Similar to The Wedding Veil series, each movie centers on a different friend and their Christmas romance. The first one, Unwrapping Christmas: Tina’s Miracle, stars Natalie Hall as the titular Tina Mitchell, the owner of said gift-wrapping shop. She finds herself in a bind after the Christmas gala she’s planning is nearly canceled until she teams up with an estate company owner to save the venue.

Of course, Hallmark is no stranger to plots about saving a business or building in time for the holidays. And the network has been criticized for being too formulaic. That being said, Tina’s Miracle is still a great watch because it sets up the rest of the movies and her own love life. She’s hesitant to open up because of a past breakup, but ultimately, she and Michael (Alec Santos) team up to save the historic venue Alford House. With some twists and turns included, it’s perfect.

The second and third movies, Mia’s Prince with Kathryn Davis and Lily’s Destiny with Ashley Newbrough, are definitely fun watches and can get anyone into the spirit. However, I do love the fourth movie, Olivia’s Reunion, which sees gift-wrapping expert Olivia (Cindy Busby) getting snowed in with her ex while delivering gifts ahead of the gala. I am a sucker for a good enemies-to-lovers plot, especially if said enemies were previously together. Putting the characters in a closed space for an undisclosed amount of time, you never know what could happen. Plus, Jake Epstein, who plays the ex, has a soft spot in my heart after portraying Craig Manning on Degrassi: The Next Generation.

All four Unwrapping Christmas movies ultimately premiered on Hallmark Channel in July 2025, but seeing that they are Hallmark+ exclusives, I couldn’t help but relive them. Fans can relive those movies and plenty more Hallmark favorites on Hallmark+. Countdown to Christmas is far from over, and there is a movie for everyone.

Passionate writer. Obsessed with anything and everything entertainment, specifically movies and television. Can get easily attached to fictional characters.

#3557. The 12 Best Gifts For RPG Lovers In 2026

I think it must be pretty hard to buy gifts for folks who love RPGs if you yourself are not familiar with them, because as I’ve discovered today while perusing the internet for ideas, most searches for RPG-themed gifts get you into the territory of tabletop RPGs rather than video game RPGs. Don’t get me wrong, I love a good TTRPG, but sometimes that’s not what you’re looking for exactly.

This is a guide to shopping for the RPG-lover in your life, someone who you know really likes a good role-playing video game with stats that go up as you level up, a nice big fantasy world of some sort, stuff you can equip to make yourself stronger, probably a party of heroes adventuring together, and possibly some interesting moments where you can make choices that influence what happens next. There are a lot of games that fall into this category, and the RPG-lover in your life may or may not like some or all of these. So as with all gifts, try to get to know the person you’re gifting something to just a little and make sure you’re getting, say, a game for a system they actually own, or a piece of merchandise for one they already played and liked.

With that in mind, here you are! 12 ideas!

Don’t worry, this list won’t be all straight-up games, but I did want to sprinkle a few recent releases in here to hopefully give you some options of newer games to gift that might broaden your giftee’s horizons. Trails in the Sky 1st ChapterÂ is a remake, released last year, of the original Trails in the Sky, which is the start of an excellent RPG that’s nonetheless (I think) overlooked by a lot of general RPG fans. The remake itself looks really nice, and the music is incredible. If you know someone who already has 1st Chapter in their library, 2nd Chapter came out this year too!

I’m not a huge collector of video game-themed merchandise, especially stuff that’s really obviously “gamer”, you know? But I have to admit these towels get me every time. It’s a genuinely funny play on a death screen from an iconic RPG series that anyone who’s touched a Souls game will probably find at least somewhat amusing.

The Adventures of Elliot is another release from this year, and while it’s not my personal favorite RPG, it’s got a lot going for it and a ton of RPG fans seemed to really dig it. Not a traditional turn-based RPG, this game instead has a singular main character, Elliot, who can switch between several different weapon types in action combat to dispatch monsters. It’s got that gorgeous HD-2D look that Square Enix has been using to marry a retro feel with modern visuals, and a pretty interesting story involving time travel to see the same world across multiple eras.

I’ve been seeing these little music boxes around for a bunch of different games, and I think they’re a really neat idea. But for an RPG fan, the absolute safest and best bet for a theme they’ll recognize is one from Final Fantasy. FF7 has several different ones, including both Tifa and Aerith’s themes, and there are more on the Square Enix store if you want to check that out or look for a music box for a specific game.

I tried to recommend several different kinds of RPGs on this list, depending on what the RPG gamer in your life most often plays. Beast of Reincarnation is a new game from the Pokemon developers, out this year, but it’s a far cry from what Pokemon is. Instead of capturing monsters, you and a single creature partner fight off blight-diseased enemies and explore a post-apocalyptic world using nature-based powers. It’s a game about humans, nature, and human nature, and might appeal especially to fans of the NieR games on aesthetic alone.

Hell yeah I’m recommending a dang notebook and pen. Who doesn’t love these? Seriously. As an RPG lover I frequently end up taking notes while playing games, either to solve puzzles, remember who the heck characters with fancy names are, or just doodling. And there are so many very cool notebooks and pens out there! You can go two directions with this. You can get something that has a very fantastical outward appearance, like this journal, or you could get a really nice-quality, plain notebook (the paper quality on this one is excellent and feels good to write on). For pens, you could get some colorful gel pens (everyone loves colors) or get a little fancy with it and introduce them to the world of fountain pens. This fountain pen is inexpensive and totally fineâif they really get into them, they may want to upgrade on a future holiday, but keep it simple for now.

This is coming out on December 3, so in just a few days: it’s Xenoblade 3 on Switch 2! Xenoblade 3 is already an excellent game, its Switch 2 version will include a new recruitable character and a quest to obtain them, a new battle mode, newly-voiced event scenes, and it’s in 4K with a glorious 60fps. Check in first to see if the person already has this game on Switch, though, as the upgrade pack by itself to the Switch 2 edition is admittedly a bit cheaper.

I love video game cookbooks. The ones by author Chelsea Monroe-Cassel are responsible for teaching me to cook in the first place! My two favorites of hers are the World of Warcraft Official Cookbook (and its sequel, New Flavors of Azeroth) and The Elder Scrolls Cookbook. All three are fun, easy to follow for novice cooks, and the recipes you end up with are both tasty and unique, often introducing me to ingredients I had never used before. The photography is also lovely, so even if your giftee doesn’t cook, they make a nice collector’s item for fans of the games. If neither of these games appeal, there’s a whole host of other video game cookbooks out there to choose from.

I dunno, I just wish someone would buy this for me. It’s cute and, if you like Undertale, actually extremely funny. Trust me, you’ll know if the RPG fan in your life likes Undertale.

I’m genuinely not sure what it is, but every time I go to Japan for work, someone asks me to get them one of these Dragon Quest slimes. They come in several different versions at varying prices, so take your pick if you know someone who loves Dragon Quest.

Oh my God. These…are hilarious. For those who loved last year’s hit RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, these slippers are sure to get a laugh when unwrapped. They’re a hilarious tribute to a character who was obsessed with collecting monster feet, and they look extremely comfy to boot. Possibly a good gift even if someone didn’t play Expedition 33 on sheer utility.

Yeah, really. I’m personally ambivalent about getting gift cards, as if that’s all you’re getting someone it can seem a tad thoughtless. But if you’re shopping for a kid who’s getting multiple things, or a secret Santa you don’t know well, this can be an okay choice. A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever RPG has been on their wishlist (though you can also just peek at their wishlist and buy one for them). You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles for those that own them. Take your pick.

#3556. Marvel's Iron Man might be planning to rear its head at The Game Awards, if EA Motive's updated website is any indication

EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.

Redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.

A new website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

For one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio said earlier this month.

Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

Second is the fact that The Game Awards air on 10th December - eight days before the global opening of Avengers: Doomsday, a film that's shaping up to become the biggest cinematic event since the last time Marvel chucked all of its toys into the same sandbox and bashed them together. Giving one of the company's most popular superheroes the spotlight around the same time seems like a good idea.

This isn't the first time EA's Iron Man has popped up in recent times, either. What appeared to be an unfinished trailer for Motive's Iron Man leaked onto the internet this summer, and showed off blisteringly fast flying and lots of destructive gadgets. It looked further along than I expected, at least, so I wouldn't be surprised to see the billionaire playboy philanthropist rear his head again in two weeks time.

#3555. Should There Be Restrictions On Game Streaming? The Japanese Producer For Danganronpa Thinks So

DanganronpaParanormasightSpike ChunsoftSquare Enix

It could be argued thatÂ Grand Theft Auto V became such a long-running phenomenon thanks to the success of GTA Online and its popularity as a game with streamers. Grand Theft Auto VI has also been dominating on streaming websites since its release, alongside beingÂ the biggest gaming launch of all time. Given this, you might assume all would agree that streaming is great for gaming, but there are still some Japanese developersâespecially in the realms of visual novels and story-driven gamesâwho feel differently. In a country where the legal landscape for streaming is very different to that seen in the West, not all agree on how to approach the topic, as seen during a conversation between the producers of two recent hits of the genre in Japan: Paranormasightâs Kazuma Oushu and Danganronpaâs Shohei Sakakibara.

Itâs worth understanding the context of game streaming in Japan, and attempts by studios to limit how much of a game can be streamed on platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Often, the release of a story-driven Japanese game can be accompanied by guidelines that allow streamers to play the games, but doesn’t permit them to post content beyond a certain chapter to prevent spoilers, sometimes years after release. This happened with Danganronpa, and Atlus have done similar with titles like Persona, only lifting restrictions on 2019’s Persona 5 Royal in 2023. They can be temporary, or permanent, and at times can lead to legal consequences (at least in Japan) or video takedowns if not followed. Globally, despite streaming games technically counting as an infringement of copyright, the concept has generally been accepted and is even embraced by developers, but less so in Japan. This is why, when streamers attached to agencies such as Hololive want to broadcast some games, they will often engage in licensing arrangements.

Even Nintendo once tried to enforce such restrictions globally. The argument is that streaming could hurt sales, especially for story-driven titles, despite there being little evidence to support this. At Japanese gaming developer conference CEDEC+Kyushu, as reported by Gamer (via Automaton Media), the creators behind Danganronpa and Paranormasight debated the merits of such restrictions, with differing opinions. Danganronpa‘s Sakakibara sees such limitations as an obvious block against destroying the core appeal of a murder mystery by giving away the answers. âIf you find out who the culprit is beforehand, half the fun is gone,â he explains. âWho would want to play a mystery when they already know the culprit? I absolutely donât want to take that experience away from players.â

Yet 2023’s Square Enix visual novel Paranormasaight is arguably proof that spoilers may not hurt sales, even for story-driven games. This mystery adventure game limited streamers from sharing just the final chapter online, and lifted this after less than a month. Oushu said that streaming helped raise awareness for the game. âThe people who are going to buy the game will buy it even if all the tricks get revealed in a video,â he claimed.

It can especially help in long-term sales after a gameâs launch, Oushu argued. People attracted to the unique visuals and setting would forget about the specific spoilers but remember being intrigued by its world by the time it went on sale, he suggested. They would see it as âan interesting game that, if it goes on sale, Iâll play itâ, Oushu added, boosting its success in the long run. Heavier restrictions, he argued, wonât allow players that sense of discovery. It also helped sales for the more recently released sequel: some who watched videos of the first game would go on to play the sequel themselves, without watching streaming content beforehand.

The debate on game streaming has mostly been settled. Today, Twitch is one of the biggest online video platforms, Nintendo lifted restrictions many years ago, and influencers are a key part of promoting almost every modern game released today. But there is still the argument it could hurt smaller and niche titles, and both producers acknowledged the relatively lower prices of their games as factors in their success despite streaming.

#3553. ArcheAge Chronicles developer XL Games faces major layoffs and possible closure after disappointing sales

XL Games, the South Korean studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles, is planning a major restructuring and has not ruled out closing altogether after the game failed to meet sales expectations.

As reported by Korean outlet Money Today Broadcasting (MTN), translated by machine, CEO Choi Kwan-ho told staff in a letter on 26th November that the company would first ask for voluntary redundancies before moving on to compulsory layoffs.

"Criticisms regarding ArcheAge Chronicles' lack of polish despite its long development period, as well as complaints concerning bugs, gameplay, and optimisation, continue to persist," Choi wrote, according to MTN. "Sales are also showing a downward trend, and we anticipate revenue that will fall far short of expectations."

Choi said XL Games will try to address some of those problems in a December update, to see whether that turns things around.

"However, the company is currently at a critical crossroads where we must even consider the possibility of going out of business," he added.

To keep the company afloat, Choi said XL Games would need to "drastically" cut back its operations and focus on essential functions with a minimal workforce. He also promised to do everything possible to make sure staff leaving the company receive their severance pay and benefits, despite the "immense financial pressure" the studio is under.

ArcheAge Chronicles launched on 3rd November, 13 years after the original ArcheAge, and is described as a seamless open-world sandbox action RPG. According to MTN, it had a production budget of around £57 million (100 billion won), and sold roughly 100,000 copies in its first 10 days. That works out to about £2.3 million (4 billion won) in gross revenue before Steam's cut, which MTN says isn't enough to sustain the studio.

It currently has a "mixed" user score, with players complaining about the combat, the speed (or lack thereof) of upgrading, lack of polish, and QoL issues. Players were also incredibly unhappy that a pre-order bonus costume was only available for one character.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the game had a troubled development. XL Games founder Song Jae-kyung - who previously led production at NCSoft and created the original ArcheAge - left the studio partway through, and the project changed direction several times.

Shockingly for a series that just released its ‘sixth’ entry, there are seven Grand Theft Auto games that never made it to PC. Seven! And what’s even more incredible is that all seven of them are stone-cold classics, apart from about six of them.

Essentially if it came to a handheld/is the biggest game release of the decade, then Rockstar hasn’t brought it to PC. I’ve ranked all the games we so unjustly missed out on. The good, the bad, and the Toni-Cipriani’s-face-levels-of-ugly. Who’s Toni, you ask, and is he really so hideous? Read on and find out!

Well, top marks for trying. Unfortunately the city is more lifeless than the set of 28 Years Later. If you somehow manage to find anyone to commit a crime against and then walk anywhere with a wanted rating, you’re instantly arrested with seemingly no way of fighting back or escaping. Driving is borderline tolerable, until you inevitably get stuck on any of the scenery. Still, some of the music goes entertainingly hard. The song the cab drivers are listening to is so intense that Travis Bickle would be recommending a therapist. Anyway, this is awful.

Why no PC port? This disaster has been so rightly lost to time that I didn’t even know it existed when I pitched this list feature.

Last year’s game except now with a populated city. Horrible driving controls are far more forgivable now that I finally have pedestrians to run over. The chiptune music is genuinely great and this time only plays when you’re inside cars (immersion!). I honestly got some borderline-entertaining police chases out of this.

Why no PC port? The grimdark PC gaming scene of the new millennium tragically couldn’t allow a soundtrack full of upbeat bangers like this.

While the music isn’t as brilliant as GTA 2 for GBC (the new metric I’m judging all videogame soundtracks by) this is an improvement in basically every way. Nicer car handling with a tight handbrake that makes up for the fact that you’re so zoomed in you’ll have to use it every three seconds not to crash into anything. We even get a story this time, laughably crap though it is.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Still, there’s a nagging sense that if Rockstar had truly committed to the GBA they might have made something genuinely excellent. But considering what the competition was attempting on this console at the time it could have been a whole lot worse.

Why no PC port? There’s far more pimps than sex workers on the streets, and us PC gamers don’t care for such lopsided bubble economies.

You know you’re in for a rough ride when there’s pop-in in the opening cutscene. Lead character Vic ‘boo hoo hoo my brother’s sick’ Vance is also a dud for the ages. When he’s not whining about his sickly sibling (yawn) he’s moaning about how much he hates crime, before unquestioningly smashing up storefronts or slaughtering hundreds for whichever psychopath asks.

You’re helping out wife-beaters and animal-on-animal voyeurs that even Trevor Philips would find a bit much. Get over that and you’ll find a beautiful take on Vice City with an impeccable eighties soundtrack. Still just about worth playing then, though maybe make sure there’s no witnesses or proof that you did.

Why no PC port? Rockstar couldn’t find a PR willing to explain why an NPC gleefully watching a video of animals banging is actually a very clever satirical comment on the American dream.

What if Pinocchio had wished to be a real boy, but the blue fairy had turned out to be a talentless hack? You’d end up with Toni Cipriani’s undead nightmare of a face. The only reason he hasn’t turned the gun on his own hideous mug is that the shooting controls in his game are equally as horrid.

But! This first PSP go is still a terrific attempt to squeeze a full fat 3D GTA into a handheld. It’s got sharp writing and characters, along with some of the funniest radio stations in the whole series. Poor shooting’s a shame, but carjacking and pedestrian-pulping is as fun as ever. And if you’re emotionally devastated about the lack of sex workers in GTA6 - yes you are you lying pervert - you can frequently enjoy running over their customers in this. Lovely.

Why no PC port? No amount of DLSS 5 could yassify Toni’s face into something acceptable to the human eye.

Always dismissed top-down old school GTA? I’m confident this DS masterclass can make a convert out of you. Rockstar expertly uses the touchscreen to give old staples a shot in the arm. Unscrewing panels and twisting wires together to hotwire a car under pressure is basically exactly what it feels like to steal a car IRL (before you disagree in the comments, keep in mind I’m also wearing a wire).

One mission has you stealing a street racer’s car to sabotage it so it blows up at the start of the race, and you even get to slap a rotten fish on the air conditioner just to really add insult to injury.

There’s an entire drug-dealing economy in it, which I’m sure Nintendo were delighted by. Blowing up security cameras - with molotov cocktails you make by sloppily pouring gasoline into bottles with the touchscreen, natch - is fun in itself. That it also subtly lowers drug prices because the police are now able to see less crimes is a level of detail I just didn’t expect on DS. More fool me.

Am I going to claim it’s got the best police chases in the entire series? Yes, and with almost a straight face too. You’re encouraged to ram cop cars and force them into collisions, taking them out Burnout-style with an immensely satisfying big red X crossing through their shattered remains. A million times more fun than the usual tedious car hide-and-seek. Plus nothing livens up trying to escape the cops in a stolen ambulance like having to simultaneously press the patient’s heart repeatedly on the touchscreen to defibrillate him back to life. The best of the top-down GTA’s by far, and puts a fair few of the fully 3D ones to shame too.

Why no PC port? When I go to Heaven for putting this game at number one, that’s the first thing I’ll be asking God.

Abbie was a staff writer on Official Xbox Magazine during the Xbox One years, and yet still persisted with games journalism. When she’s not blowing her meagre savings on every handheld PC she can get her grubby mitts on, she writes for Edge, GamesRadar, Retro Gamer, and of course PC Gamer. Otherwise she’s likely losing herself to a roguelike deckbuilder, yelling at you about another excellent detective game, or wondering what else she could have done with the 300 hours of her life that she’s lost to Mewgenics.

#3551. After Persona 6, You (Probably) Won’t Have To Wait A Decade For Persona 7

A decade has passed since the initial release of Persona 5, all the way back in 2016. While Atlusâs Persona Studio was able to release Metaphor Re:Fantazio in the interim, the studios’s core franchise has subsisted only on remakes and spin-offs, developed by external studios. Good news though: According to an interview with Waku Wada for SEGA Sammyâs official corporate site, itâs likely that the wait between Persona 6 and Persona 7 wonât be quite as long.

The wide-ranging interview covers much of the Persona franchise’s history, including discussing the jump in success the series enjoyed following the 2006 release of Persona 3. This, Wada argued, was due to broadening the game’s potential appeal, while maintaining its core elements, all at a precarious time for publishers Atlus.

At the time of Persona 3âs development, the industry was in a decline, and Atlus was in a difficult financial situation that was felt across the entire development team. Amidst this, there was a feeling that if the game didnât sell, we wouldnât be able to keep making games, so development was approached almost like weâd been pushed into a corner. Until then, we would create the edgy titles we wanted to make, and these would be well-received and supported by a dedicated fanbase. We believed that was enough. However, as the industry began to decline, unless we reached a wider audience, those efforts would be over.

The game found success by going against the trend for realism, evolving the anime expressionism and psychological ideas of prior games and putting them in a more appealing setting. A few years later Persona 4 was built on the same groundwork, and the series grew even more thanks to the release of Persona 5 and its expansion, Royal. Wada also acknowledged the effect of bringing the franchise to online stores. âA major turning point was the release of the Steam version of Persona 4: The Golden,â he explained. âWe had long been discussing porting our games internally with a view to expanding the global market, and once the timing was right, we launched the game on there worldwide simultaneously in 2020 with support for many languages. It surpassed one million copies sold in just one year.â

It was that success which led to the company pushing ahead with Persona 5 on Steam and doing more worldwide simultaneous releases. Nowadays, through remakes and concerts, the series has found multimedia success on a global scale, but the wait for a wholly new entry goes on. However, the studio is actively refining its efforts to ensure that such long waits wonât become the norm. âPersona 6 is not the end goal,â Wada said. âWeâre putting in a lot of effort to ensure that fans wonât have to wait a long time for the next installment like before. To keep developing Persona into an even larger series, weâre also constantly thinking about concepts and story ideas that wonât disappoint expectations.â He clarified that faster development comes through greater collaboration between teams, and building systems that can be reused. There’s also an effort to pool veteran knowledge with series information that even the team has forgotten but fans can remember, all to ensure they donât need to remake elements with every entry.

Wada seems certain that, after so many years waiting for Persona 6, we wonât be waiting another decade for Persona 7. And who knows, if the rumored Persona 1 remake is real and can bridge the gap between releases, the wait may feel like nothing at all.

#3550. An easy-to-miss GTA 6 scene sheds new light on Mandy and Jason

Mandy was one of GTA 6's breakout characters almost as soon as the game launched, but it's only now that we're learning how her obsession with Jason may have come to be.

As spotted by IGN, an easy-to-miss line of dialogue suggests the pair do have some kind of history. It's heard during one of Lucia's meditation sequences, which replay snippets from a character's past, usually centred on their insecurities.

In this particular sequence, Lucia recalls a conversation with Jason that seems to have taken place off-screen.

"Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago," Jason says. "You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again."

Jason doesn't name Mandy, but IGN reckons the context makes it pretty clear who he's talking about. As he mentions not wanting to lose Lucia again, it believes the conversation took place after the couple first split up, and after Lucia's release from prison, when she was living in the same neighbourhood as Mandy.

That would also explain why Lucia is so clearly aware of Mandy. At the end of Chapter 1, while fleeing Jason's house as Lucia, players can find Mandy giving the police a statement, in which she exaggerates how close she and Jason were. If players step out of hiding, Lucia confronts her directly: "Stay the fu*k away from Jason, you crazy bitch."

LUCIA FINDS OUT ABOUTMANDY & GOES CRAZY 🤯#GTA6 #GTAVI pic.twitter.com/nTEDFb3PA8

The same encounter adds weight to fan theories that Mandy is hiding something far darker, as she tells police she "wanted to light [Jason's] house on fire so many times".

Mandy actress Lexie Shoaibi has since spoken about her "bittersweet" newfound fame, revealing that people keep trying to impersonate her on social media. She also said she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, and voiced several other NPCs while working with Rockstar.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.
