Major spoilers for the Blade Runner 2099 finale, “Share the Fantasy” lie ahead.

Blade Runner 2099 has finally arrived, delivering eight dystopian and drama-filled installments that deftly build upon the mythology of the beloved sci-fi franchise. The show follows dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and desperate Replicant imitator Cora (Hunter Schafer), who eventually uncover a long-held secret regarding the Tyrell Corporation. This all culminates into quite a finale, and Schafer and series creator Silka Luisa spoke to CinemaBlend about THAT final Cora scene.

Ahead of “Share the Fantasy,” Cora has learned that her adoptive mother, Helena (Sheila Atim) was actually a Nexus-1 Replicant, who was killed by fellow Nexus 1 model Julius (Tom Burke). It turns out the memory belongs to Replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and holds the process of producing the (longer living) Nexus-1s. Olwen and Cora head to an Tyrell Off-World Launch complex, where the former wants to receive more time to live and the latter aims to get the memory back from Julius, who wants the sole power to create Replicants.

Ultimately, Julius destroys the memory and is killed shortly after by his bloodthirsty cohort, Clotilde (Amy Lennox), who he transformed into a Nexus-1 and left in the dark about certain details. Amid the chaos, Cora is also seriously injured and seemingly near death. Clotilde then reveals to Olwen that she knows how to produce Nexus-1s and offers it to Olwen to repay her for saving her life earlier. While someone is later turned into a Nexus-1, it’s unclear who it is, as viewers only see a hand coming out of a pod.

In the final scene of this 2026 TV schedule entry, Olwen is seen exploring planets off world but, before that,, Cora returns to the Replicant police station, where she undergoes another Voight-Kampff human-detection evaluation by Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey). While Cora fails, she seems more calculating and emotionally tests Greta with her own responses. It’s a well-acted and complex scene, so I had to ask the creative team about it.

Needless to say, the Cora scene – like the finale as a whole – leaves viewers with a lot to chew on. Showrunner Silka Luisa, a longtime fan of the Blade Runner franchise, wouldn’t give any specific answers about the last moment with Cora. However, during her conversation with CinemaBlend, she did acknowledge her thoughts on why viewers would likely have differing thoughts about it:

Blade Runner always has an ambiguous ending, and so I think part of what I'm really proud of in the show is that you come to the end and that people can have different interpretations about what that final scene means to them, and they can imagine, just like you asked me on 2049…. They can fill in that with their own story.

While 2099 doesn’t have any direct ties to the events of the films, it does indeed follow in their footsteps by providing an ambiguous ending. So I completely agree with Luisa that it’ll spark differing interpretations from viewers. And, just as I probed Luisa for her take on Rick Deckard’s post-2049 fate, I also directly asked whether Cora would just masquerade as a Replicant moving forward. The EP would only say this to me:

We can't answer that question, but I can tell [you] I loved writing it. But I mean, [Hunter and I] didn't even talk that much about it. Hunter just came on set, and she felt so different. I mean, you just came on and just nailed it. It was one of those things where I like, my jaw hit the floor. She's so phenomenal in that scene.

There’s so much to consider in the scene, including the notion that Cora may have actually undergone the Nexus-1 process and become a Replicant herself. Alas, Schafer avoided giving any specifics on that, but she did speak highly of her experience filming the scene and how it differed from much of her time on set:

I loved that scene because it — well, I mean, also at that point in filming, like by Episode 8, you know, I'm not really having to think too much about character work anymore at that point. She's in me, and I can just sort of drop into her. I love when you reach that point in filming, but it was fun because it felt like a different Cora in a different sort of energetic place. And so I think we just had fun filming it. Also, [director] Ariel [Kleiman] was super down to play with it. Yeah, I mean, it's hard to talk about. It's so wild talking about it now.

This show succeeds in delivering impressive visuals, strong performances and brutal action, though I also applaud Silka Luisa and her staff for adding some fresh elements to the franchise. And, while I would love to have some concrete answers regarding the final moments of this limited series, a part of me certainly respects Luisa’s desire to let the audience made up their own mind about the finer details.

Blade Runner 2099 is now available to stream with a Prime Video subscription.

#3548. Call of Duty movie will "probably" feature Captain Price

Captain Price will "probably" pop up in the upcoming Call of Duty film.

That's according to the movie's director, Peter Berg, who told Variety that the film will be based on the Modern Warfare universe and hinted that its best-known British soldier will be in it.

"We've already said that we're basing it on the 'Modern Warfare' universe," Berg said. "So you can probably expect to see Captain Price, I would think."

Admittedly, that "probably" is doing a lot of heavy lifting, but it feels more like a gentle tease than an intentional misdirection.

Price was first introduced in the original Call of Duty and later became a series mainstay, most recently in the Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare remake.

Berg also revealed that casting is now underway, so we could hear more about who's starring in the coming months, although no actors have been announced yet.

Paramount Pictures is producing the film in partnership with Activision. Berg is directing and co-writing, with Taylor Sheridan attached to write the screenplay. It's due to release on 30th June 2028.

Grand Theft Auto 6 money glitches were inevitable, but until now the supposed "glitches" weren't really glitches at all. The most popular methods involve looting a location and forcing the loot to respawn, which is less of a glitch and more of a quirk of how the game works.

The new GTA 6 money glitch is clearly not how the game should work. Reddit user MichaelOrSum was the first person I saw who found a way to make up to $1M in a few minutes. There's no swapping characters or forcing loot to respawn required here: You just need access to one of GTA 6's fence locations if you're in chapter 1 or 2 (there's a way around it in chapter 3).

Most people recommend finding a winched vehicle and stealing an ATM to pull this glitch off, but you can also just visit the location of the old GTA 6 infinite money glitch. The goal is to get your hands on a stash bag with some kind of stolen goods in it.

The next part will sound fake, but, trust me, it works. I gave it a shot myself and walked away with $30,000 in under a minute.

Here are the exact steps for the new GTA 6 money glitch:

For whatever reason, when your character picks the stash bag up while crouched the money value doubles. I've never carried around stolen drugs, but I'm pretty sure this isn't how it's supposed to work.

People in the original Reddit thread report that sometimes you can't pick the bag up. The solution to that is to swap to your other character and have them perform the money glitch. Otherwise, you'll need to start over by reloading a save or finding another stash bag. Apparently, marked bills (which cap out at $320K) are less prone to this than other stolen goods.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Reddit user angryPirate12 adds that keeping a glitched stash bag on your shoulder while in a stolen van and registering it at a Pay 'n' Spray will fill all 10 storage slots with stash bags of the same value. "I have over $10 million in my vans in less than 30 mins," they said.

I will note that most of GTA 6's story is about doing jobs for money, so filling up your bank account might ruin the fun of watching the numbers go up as Jason and Lucia's crimes escalate. Once you're pretty deep into the later chapters, money isn't much of an issue anyway, and there isn't a whole lot to spend it on. So, money glitch responsibly, is all I'm saying.

I’ve been looking forward to the release of the Meet the Parents movie, Focker In-Law, all year. However, following its premiere on the 2026 movie schedule, it’s been met with a pretty rough Rotten Tomatoes score of 32%. While that might be a scary number to see, I’m here to tell you I think you should ignore it and focus on some other figures.

At the time of this writing, Focker In-Law’s Tomatometer score is sitting at 32% based on 95 reviews. And when you look at the blurbs from reviews featured on Rotten Tomatoes, they are not complimentary.

Michael Cook from KLRT-TV wrote that while it’s a comedy, “what’s missing are the laughs.” ScreenRant’s Liz Declan thought that the movie wanted to side-step the two sequels that came before it, but “sadly” “offers much of the same.” According to Gabrielle Moss at Collider, there’s “just not much left to milk” here. And Brett Arnold from Yahoo wrote that even though he thinks this is the best Focker film, it still “settles for a low hum of ‘cute enough’ antics.”

So, even though this movie got some fresh reviews, overwhelmingly, Focker In-Law fell into the rotten category for the critics on Rotten Tomatoes.

Now, I’m always of the opinion that you should make up your mind for yourself with a movie. So, yes, obviously, you should go see Focker In-Law. However, there are also some numbers we can point to that signify there is a group of people who do really like this movie.

First of all, the audience score for Focker In-Law is great. It sits at an 86% based on over 250 reviews. Overall, I’d say that’s a pretty stellar Popcornmeter score, and a sign that this movie is a crowd-pleaser.

Also, it’s worth noting that at the time of this writing, Focker In-Law actually has a higher audience score than Meet the Parents. While the OG movie starring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro has an 85% from critics, making it the highest-reviewed film in this franchise, it has a 79% on the Popcornmeter. Of course, Focker In-Law’s numbers can fluctuate as reactions continue to pour in. However, right now, according to audiences, it’s comparable to the original.

I, personally, also really enjoyed the flick. As a fan of the original movies, I thought Focker In-Law was a very fun film that referenced the Meet the Parents movies in clever ways, while also providing a fresh take on the early 2000s comedy. Plus, I’ll take any opportunity I can to see Ariana Grande flex her comedy chops, and I loved watching Ben Stiller and Skyler Gisondo play father and son again.

Along with the numbers I cited above, I think it’s worth noting that Meet the Parents' first sequel, Meet the Fockers (which you can stream with a Peacock subscription), has a significantly worse audience score than Focker In-Law. It sits at 58% on the Popcornmeter, which is shocking to me considering I know plenty of people who love Meet the Fockers. Along with that, the sequel’s critics' score is 39%, which is only a little bit higher than Focker In-Law’s score.

So, all this is to say, maybe don’t think too hard about that 32%. Clearly, there are folks who have loved Focker In-Law, and as one of those people, I wholeheartedly believe it’s worth a trip to the movie theater.

And just to throw it out there, I also think it's worthy of a sequel. What can I say? I want to meet Ariana Grande’s parents.

#3544. No Man's Sky's QSSR upgrade on PS5 is "night and day", says Hello Games developer

Hello Games has confirmed that its procedurally generated space sim, No Man's Sky, is getting a major visual upgrade on PS5 as it swaps its existing upscaling for Sony's new Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) tech.

Hello Games' engine programmer Martin Griffiths shared the news on X/Twitter, calling the difference "night and day".

"Replacing our older FSR-based upscaling with QSSR provides a substantial boost in image quality - it's night and day when you see it in person!" Griffiths wrote. "As always, it was super fun to work closely with Sony on a new technology like this."

No Man's Sky was one of several games Sony named earlier this month as receiving QSSR support, alongside Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Control Resonant, The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam. According to the PlayStation Blog, the updates are rolling out over the coming weeks.

QSSR support for PS5 is incoming for #NoMansSky : As always, it was super fun to work closely with Sony on a new technology like this. Replacing our older FSR-based upscaling with QSSR provides a substantial boost in image quality – it’s night and day when you see it in person!… pic.twitter.com/ExHBrYpHzA

"No Man's Sky gives players an infinite procedural universe to explore. When every star in the night sky is a real solar system players can visit, we care a great deal about the quality of every pixel," Hello Games founder Sean Murray said in the post.

"QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution) allows us to render the universe in sharper, cleaner and more beautiful detail, while delivering the best possible framerate. Look for it in the next few weeks."

QSSR brings AI-guided upscaling to the standard PS5, and is built on the same foundation as the PS5 Pro's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). Sony says it delivers "sharper details, cleaner edges, and more stable images than traditional upscalers". Like the upgraded PSSR, it grew out of Project Amethyst, Sony's ongoing collaboration with AMD.

ICYMI, iPhone and iPad owners finally get to boldly go into No Man's Sky's procedurally generated universe. But developer Hello Games recently said it wasn't stopping there, confirming it was also launching a new update, Forsaken, for all players, bringing a bit of seasonal spookiness to the exploratory space sim.

Eurogamer recently spoke to the No Man's Sky players building utopia at the end of the universe.

#3543. Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a New Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

So we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in New York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a big turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

#3542. 11 Gifts To Buy For The GTA 6 Fan In Your Life

As we approach the holiday season, we also approach the time when we all need to start buying gifts for people we know. Sometimes this can be annoying, but this year, if you have someone in your life who’s playing a ton of Grand Theft Auto 6 (and considering how many copies it’s sold, there’s a good chance you do!), there are some really easy gifts you can get them that will make them almost as happy as hanging out with Jason and Lucia.

Here are 11 gift ideas for the GTA 6 fan in your life. Just remember to figure out which console they’re playing on so you don’t get the wrong version of some of these gifts.

Assuming the GTA 6 fan in your life is playing on PS5 which, statistically speaking, is very likely, this is a fantastic option for them. Any version of this controller looks great and will let them explore Vice City in style.

Xbox doesn’t have an official GTA 6 controller, but you can find a really nice pink controller on sites like Amazon and Walmart. Just make sure you’re buying an officially branded Xbox controller and not some cheap knock-off that won’t feel good to use and will likely break after a few weeks. I’ve heard good things about this PowerA Vice City-inspired controller, but it uses a dongle or wire to connect, so keep that in mind.

Rockstar sells a variety of Grand Theft Auto 6 merch, like shirts and hats, on its official online store. If you aren’t sure what to get, I’ve got some of this stuff already, and I can easily recommend the tote bags. They’re well made, look cool, and are big enough to actually be useful while out and about. The shirts are also well made, but sizing runs small, so keep that in mind.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has some incredible music in it, and many of the game’s tracks were created just for GTA 6, includingÂ the banger opening song “Starting From Zero.” Any GTA 6 fan is going to be listening to these songs on repeat for some time, so why not buy them a nice version of the album? Sure, you can listen to it digitally, but for the real GTA 6 fans out there, owning a physical copy of the album will be a treat. And if they’re into vinyl, you can buy them this awesome-looking version of the GTA 6 album.

Speaking of physical copies of the game, perhaps buy them a boxed copy of GTA 6. It’s true, it doesn’t come with a disc, but if they bought the game digitally, they don’t have a physical object to hold onto. They also don’t have a cool paper map, either. And if you want, you can just take the code from inside; they don’t need it, so you can keep it for yourself if you’ve yet to buy GTA 6.Â

They might already have the game, but they might not have purchased the $100 version of GTA 6. So figure that out, and if they haven’t, buy them a $20 PSN or Xbox card so they can upgrade to the Ultimate Edition and check out all the extra cosmetic goodies available in-game.

Admittedly, this isn’t the best way to play the original Vice City. But it is a very easy way to play the original Vice City. And the GTA 6 fans in your life might be craving a trip to the original Vice City right now. With the Definitive Edition, which includes GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas, they can easily play the older games on the console and TV that they play GTA 6 on already. So while these remakes weren’t perfect, they’re convenient and can be bought physically, so you can wrap them up and pop them under the tree.

After playing a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6, I wanted to re-watch some classic crime movies. And at the top of my list were two all-timers set in Miami: Scarface and 2006’s Miami Vice.Â These can be found on Blu-ray pretty easily. If the GTA 6 fan in your life owns a PS5 or Xbox Series X console with a disc drive, you can buy them the 4K UHD version of Scarface. And next month, Miami Vice finally gets a director’s cut 4KUHD release. Perfect timing.

Yeah, sure, it’s not a GTA game, but Watch Dogs 2 is the closest Ubisoft ever got to matching the level of detail and fun found in actual Grand Theft Auto games. Plus, the game’s storyline about tech companies going too far and hackers fighting themselves and each other feels more relevant in 2026 than ever before.

If the GTA fan in your life loved the grounded storytelling and realistic characters of GTA 6, then I’d recommend buying them Mafia: The Old Country on their platform of choice as a gift. Mafia: The Old Country is a shorter game than GTA 6, but it offers up some truly impressive visuals and a solid story about the old mafia in Italy and how dangerous, but alluring, it could be to those wanting a better life.

Hey, I own a few of these, and I love them so much. And after playing GTA 6, I’ve been busting them out of my closet when going to the store. So why not support your GTA 6 fan’s desire to live in Vice City and buy them a nice Hawaiian shirt? You can even find places selling knock-offs of Tommy Vercetti’s iconic blue Hawaiian shirt if you look around.

This is a gift that only works if they own a PS2 or a PS3 that can play PS2 games. But if they do, then maybe pick them up a copy of Vice City Stories on PS2. This is a somewhat rare GTA in 2026, as Rockstar never ported it to any other platforms after it launched on PSP, so outside of emulation and some in-development fan PC ports, the only way to play VCS is on a PS2. The game is also a bit hard to find these days, so just owning a copy of it is pretty cool. A lot of GTA fans have never played this game and might have forgotten about it at this point. This will get you plenty of cool points on Christmas.

#3540. Lesley Manville, Pierce Brosnan, and More Celebrate Violinist Joshua Bell at the Langham London

At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” says Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”

Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” says Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”

It certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”

Bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

For actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” says Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”

And that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”

#3539. Fight The Bleak Friday Blues With 12 Incredible Indie Games To Slam On Your Wishlist

DFor centuries archaeologists have attempted to learn the origins of what we believe was known as Bleak Friday. Theories have long-pointed toward some sort of national purge day, in which citizens of the United States were encouraged to murder one another in the pursuit of widescreen televisions. But more and more evidence is being unearthed that it might have been a day of mourning due to not knowing which indie game to play next. To prevent a repeat of such a tragic era of human history, we at Kotaku 3000 are introducing preventative measures, and have compiled together 12 completely excellent lesser-known indie games to keep the bleakness away.

Or indeed, I asked developers to email me about their recently released or upcoming games that aren’t getting any attention, so I could stick them on the front page of the site while the bosses are distracted by sales. 12 such games went up on the site yesterday, and here are 12 more! I really cannot get over the incredible variety, originality and excellence on display here. Some are already out and can be bought, and the rest deserve a place on your wishlist.

Developer: Pandan Games Release date: Q2 2027 Steam

An indie game inspired byÂ Ratchet & Clank is a tall order, but it really looks like Pandan Games could do it.Â GearGrit is a third-person platformer where you play as Tansy Geargrit, escaping from prison for crimes she maybe only committed some of, and attempting to unearth a giant government conspiracy.

Developer: darqwerful Release date: TBA Steam

Detective games are having such an excellent resurgence, andÂ The Detective’s Apprentice looks to be offering a deep, pure example of the form. You play as Cleo, the niece of famous detective Maya Lynch, searching for clues and making logical deductions to solve crimes and murders. Thematically it looks to be of an Agatha Christie era, with all sorts of crime reconstruction, interviewing, information gathering, and all that good stuff. There is a demo, although no release date yet.

Developer: Sebastian Gioseffi Release date: Out now Steam

“A very short game about the very best part of video games: the menus,” reads the store description forÂ Video Game Menu: The Game. And boy, does it have a lot of menus. Menus with buttons! And toggles! And an option for “cursorphobic buttons.” There’s also an option for “looming figure” which seems a bit unsettling. And apparently a way to get a flight sim HUD. It looks wonderfully bonkers, and you can buy and play it right now.

Developer: Mothman Mothman Studios Release date: Out now Steam

I suppose you could argue thatÂ PokÃ©mon Snap is a form of cryptid cam game, butÂ CryptidCam is the real thing. This super-cute game is about taking photos of sweet little woodland oddities, including the likes of the Loch Ness Monster, bigfoot, and the Loveland Frogman (my new obsession), as well as just gorgeous beasties with extra horns. You add your photos to the Cryptid-Nomicon, all for the sake of mysterious cryptozoologist Dr. Ted Krupp, and enough of my waffle, it’s out now so I’m already installing it.

Developer: Chaparral Collective, Unspeakable Pixels Release date: 2027 Steam

Unspeakable Pixels made 2020’s utterly wonderfulÂ Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials, and you should definitely go buy and play that immediately. Do that while waiting for next year’sÂ Gift of the Primordials, a turn-based puzzle game about…balancing soil nutrients? No, come back, it looks really good! It’s about building habitats for fantasy wildlife through puzzle mechanics based around judicious placement of plants. I’m still not selling it well. Watch the trailer. And playÂ Batbarian.

Developer: Sunna Entertainment Release date: TBA Steam

Surely this can’t be the first time someone’s thought to crossÂ Tetris with a platform game? But I’ve certainly never seen it before. And hot-damn, check out the animation work in the trailer above. This just looks phenomenal, with multiple characters and loadouts, buildingÂ Tetrisy towers in order to attack enemies, build combos and gather new skills. There’s a demo to check it out right now, but no sign of a release date yet.

Developer: Gabriel Maldonado Release date: Dec 4 Steam

“Flash is fragile,” says the blurb forÂ Ad Iterum, “but you can hack it.” Eek. This top-down turn-based roguelike looks gloriously macabre, with wonderful pixel art, as you descend through dungeons mutating your own body through the devouring of your enemies. It’s about seeing how far down you dare go, before attempting to return to the surface with your ill-gotten gains, with unique combinations of mutations defining each run through the procedurally generated world. And it’s out next week!

Developer: Little Sister Games Release date: 2027 Steam

As we all know, the way through the underworld is not via well-timed combat, but through the rolling of dice.Â Lovers Die is a Yahtzee-inspired roguelite, rolling dice to eliminate categories as you build up attacks. I adore the art here, those crunchy pixels and the wonderful way descriptive text is presented. Also, why aren’t more dicebuilders based on Yahtzee?! This is a darker, more adult game that the art might initially suggest, and looks compelling. We have to wait until next year to play it.

Developer: Fe Angelo, 2dchaos Release date: TBA Steam, Itch

Oh my goodness, you have to check out how this third-person survival horror uses color. It’s stunning. I mean, everything about the art is stunning.Â NechromiaÂ is about escaping a gothic castle built of someone else’s memories, with only a lantern to protect you. This looks so incredibly promising, and there’s a demo available on the Itch page for the game.

Developer: Dagada’s Team, Matthieu Lu Release date: TBA Steam

Gosh, this immediately induced some nostalgia.Â Dagada’s Story looks deeply reminiscent of the Atari/Amiga era of 16-bit platformers, complete with a mascot-like main character. You play as Dagada and his flying chum Naou, able to control each separately in order to solve puzzles, with the goal of saving the harmony of an alien mountain in order to repair Dagada’s spaceship and get home. It looks very charming, and there’s already a demo to check out.

Developer: Stellar Cartography Interactive Release date: Out now Steam

Is it OK to decide you already like a game entirely based on the pun in its title?Â Prophet MarginÂ is part city builder, part board game and part strategy, all about creating trade routes that please the gods. The emphasis is on calm, meditative play, with lots of deep thinking and methodical planning, as well as appeasing the deities of each resource. It came out just a few weeks ago, and for those who’ve discovered it is proving very well-received, although the unfortunate closure of the intended publisher means it’s not yet found enough eyes.

Developer: Goloso Games Release date: TBA Steam

One-person team Goloso Games made 2021’s excellentÂ Inspector Waffles, a great point-and-click adventure that is well worth your time. Their next game isÂ Antenna Dilemma, a new adventure featuring C432632, a grey cube who discovers there’s more to reality than his sofa and TV. It looks superbly bizarre, and there’s a demo out there already if you want to find out more.

#3538. GTA 6 Players On PS5 Averaged 17+ Hours During First Weekend

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and it's breaking records everywhere, including at PlayStation.

The gaming giant has announced that GTA 6 is the "biggest launch in PlayStation history, a record that goes back 30+ years and five console generations. According to the gaming giant, more than 39 million unique players on PS5 have jumped into GTA 6 so far.

Here is a quick rundown of GTA 6's new records on PS5 so far (covering the November 19-22 period):

  • Highest number of concurrent players for any free or paid game on PlayStation, ahead of Fortnite, Call of Duty, and everything else.
  • Players collectively logged 683 million hours of GTA 6 at launch, with each player spending an average of 17.4 hours in the game's first few days.
  • GTA 6's launch led to the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the system came out in 2020, and outside of the Christmas season.
  • GTA 6 was the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles, which suggests a lot of people bought a system specifically for GTA 6.

A big, record-breaking start for GTA 6 was always expected. If the game didn't break records, that would be a bigger story. Additionally, GTA 6 is an anomaly--its success will not save the AAA industry from its many serious, deep-rooted issues, experts have said, and many believe other publishers will learn all the wrong lessons.

GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored.

Spoilers for Disney's Hexed are ahead! You can catch the movie in theaters now.

Disney’s newest animated film, Hexed, is all about witches. At least, that’s what I expected it to be about from all the teasers and trailers released to promote the film. For the most part, Hexed does make good on that promise. However, by the time the credits started to roll, I couldn’t help but wonder if I just watched the origin story of a new Disney princess.

Let me back up a bit, though. Hexed centers on Billie Doe, a mischievous high school student with a heart of gold who discovers she has magical powers while trying to evade her principal, who is going to expel her. Back at home, Billie opens a portal to Hexe, the magic-filled world where witches and wizards live. It’s there that she meets the Queen of Hexe, who just so happens to be her grandmother. Now, I’m not an expert on royal lineage, but I’m pretty sure being the granddaughter of the queen makes you a princess.

Here’s the thing: becoming an official Disney princess is a lot more complicated than it sounds. There are rules and requirements a character must meet before they’re even considered for the coronation. The big three are (via Movieweb): being the lead or co-lead in the movie, having a pet sidekick, being human (sorry, Nala), and having some connection to royalty or making a heroic decision (in the case of Mulan). However, even meeting all four requirements doesn’t guarantee a character a Disney crown. Just look at Frozen’s Anna and Elsa. Though, in the famous sisters’ case, Disney considers them to be more popular on their own than they would be as part of the official lineup.

All of this begs the question: Is Billie a Disney princess? She’s definitely the lead of the movie. In a way, she has two sidekicks, one in the form of the cat, Beef Roger Crummchuk, and the other in the form of the bewitched cauldron, Bucket. She may be a witch, but she’s a human witch. And not only does she have a connection to royalty through her grandmother and later her mom after she assumes the rightful role of Queen as Hexe, but she also makes a heroic move to save the world of Hexe.

Billie From Hexed Has Just Landed At Disney Parks, But The Directors Already Have Bigger Ideas

There’s no doubt that Billie has met the big four requirements. However, there is one more lesser-known requirement that has to be met for the House of Mouse to consider a character an official princess: the movie has to be a hit. In fact, the success of a movie has to extend well past its release to ensure a princess keeps her title — just look at The Hunchback of Notre Dame’s Esmerelda, who used to be in the official lineup and now is not.

Unfortunately, the early box office numbers aren’t looking too great for Hexed. I’m not too worried about Billie’s princess status, though, since plenty of recent Disney original movies have found their audiences after they’ve been released and made available for those with a Disney+ subscription. At least, that’s what I’m telling myself because I really want Billie to be Disney’s first pink-haired princess!

You can catch Disney’s Hexed in theaters now.

#3536. GTA 6 Has A Secret Mission That Feels Like Hard Target Meets Saw

In the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry.

Go to Hyde Island

Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out.

Listen to your captor's speech

Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move.

Run to the tent directly in front of you

You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers.

Search for more outposts

You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you.

Prepare for a showdown

Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off.

Collect your rewards

Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work.

What happens if you fail?

If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again.

#3535. Are the Royals More Relatable Now Than Ever?

Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to New Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a new blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, says Myers.

“William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers says.

According to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

“I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers says. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to New Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”

The visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.)

William and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

“The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

“William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader plans. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental issues and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, shows his pulling power and influence.”

#3534. Thursday Night Football Had Lowest Viewership All Season On GTA 6 Launch Day

The Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out, had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6.

The data shows that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video. That was a 9% slide from the Week 11 Thursday Night Football matchup in 2025 featuring the New England Patriots and New York Jets.

Looking at week-over-week, the November 12 matchup this year between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants drew 16.27 million viewers, and was up 17% compared to the Week 10 matchup in 2025 featuring the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos.

Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per game.

One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by a score of 26-3.

The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to.

Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations.

GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored.

Ian Somerhalder sure knows how to grab the attention of the Internet over a relaxing Thanksgiving break.

On Thursday, November 27, The Vampire Diaries actor got fans talking when he posted a shirtless photo online.

“✅Grateful for YOU ALL,” Somerhalder, 47, wrote via Instagram while posing shirtless outside the room of a home gym. “TBT and ready to get back to this in 2027! Using Absorb Co products!”

The Absorption Company is a supplement brand cofounded by Somerhalder and his wife, Nikki Reed, which focuses on increasing nutrient bioavailability.

In his social media post, the actor and businessman also said he was grateful for his Brother’s Bond Bourbon and his Groundswell film, which was released earlier this year.

“I’m so grateful for the love and support for these massive tentpole things in my life that I am building! What are you grateful for?” he asked. “Getting back to this body at 48 is going to take dedication, discipline and absorption!”

Instead of sharing what they were thankful for, many followers were quick to praise Somerhalder — who shares two children with Reed, 38 — for his physique.

“I’m grateful for the internet, which gave me the opportunity to see this picture on Thanksgiving🥵,” one fan wrote via Instagram. Another user added, “Not Ian breaking the Thanksgiving internet! ❤️❤️❤️.”

The photo even grabbed the attention of Somerhalder’s TVD costar Paul Wesley, who reportedly left a funny comment that read, “Blink twice if u need help.”

Somerhalder and Reed — who have been married since 2015 — quietly left Los Angeles to raise their kids on a California farm.

“The entertainment world really gave us these amazing platforms,” Somerhalder once told Us. “We’re super grateful for it.”

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth has Brad Pitt and director David Fincher continuing what Quentin Tarantino started on Once Upon a Time… In Hollywood on the 2026 movie schedule. And yes, Fincher brought his famed countless takes to the hangout film. When CinemaBlend spoke to one of Pitt's co-stars, she recalled how the Fight Club actor handled his longtime collaborator’s reputation on set.

After previously working together on Se7en, Fight Club and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, Brad Pitt and David Fincher reteamed for the fourth time for Cliff Booth after getting Tarantino’s blessing to adapt his script. Pitt is a veteran of Fincher’s relentless use of takes, and Carla Gugino told us about one time on set when Pitt commented on it. In her words to CinemaBlend:

I just remember at one point we were doing the master, and Brad just really sweetly looked over at the guy who was standing there as the valet who'd been there for so many hours, and he looked over, and he was like, ‘Don't worry, you will go home.’ It was really sweet. And then everybody laughed. So, I feel like that one we actually did quite a few takes.

Gugino plays Toni Peters, a former lover of Cliff Booth, whom he runs into while working with her husband, Charlie Peters (played by Scott Caan). During a scene where they talk outside a tennis club, Gugino recalled the scene requiring a lot of takes because it “involved so many elements” like a crane and cars coming and going.

Per the actress also known for Spy Kids and The Haunting of Hill House, Brad Pitt noticed one background actor and took a moment to reassure him he would “go home” at some point in between the relentless number of takes. She found it to be a “sweet” way for the actor to perhaps validate the difficulty of working on a Fincher project.

Over the years, we’ve heard all sorts of stories from other actors about David Fincher’s tendency to do a ton of takes. Ben Affleck called the process “the best film school you can go to”, whilst Charles Dance once recalled Gary Oldman getting snappy with the director for having to do one scene “a hundred fucking times” on Mank.

His new movie sees Brad Pitt’s famed Once Upon A Time… In Hollywood role (which earned him his first and only Oscar) eight years later. It also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Timothy Olyphant and Nicholas Hammond. This time, the former stuntman is approached by popular TV star Charlie Peters to help him out with a dangerous pickle he’s embroiled in.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is currently showing on IMAX screens and will be available to stream with a Netflix subscription starting on December 23. You can check out what the reviews are saying before seeing Pitt and Fincher’s latest collaboration.

#3531. GTA 6 Is Giving Pornhub A Hard Time

Not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive open-world game launched. It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the "biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4 hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a quick browse of after-hours material.

According to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later.

Thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with users searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low.

Thursday Night Football also saw a big dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's new open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.

#3530. This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before. The restaurant opened in 2024 but feels like it’s been there forever, a place with a natural hum and not an ounce of perspiration. Its clientele is specific but unpredictable; when I went there this summer for lunch with a movie producer, we spotted a powerful name-brand media executive, an architectural bigwig who designs the homes of billionaires, and a two-time Academy Award–winning actor. A few nights later, I sat near Walter Isaacson, who’s a regular. And don’t just take it from Elon Musk’s biographer. Matthew Schneier, the chief restaurant critic at New York magazine, recently named Borgo the city’s best all-around restaurant.

Read True Colors: Inside the global deals and colorful critiques that make the art world go round, with a weekly guide to the must-see openings, auctions, and fairs.

On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades. He met Ross Bleckner there, and David Salle. He used to have a massive loft studio in Williamsburg, but as rents went up, he moved deeper into Brooklyn, to Fort Greene, where he built a studio in his basement.

The twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art. That’s because he was Andrew Tarlow—the painter and restaurateur who kick-started the Brooklyn aesthetic with his restaurant Diner and, yes, also owns Borgo.

After launching that instant hit in an old, reclaimed diner, Tarlow opened five more era-defining Brooklyn spots before finally venturing into Manhattan with Borgo. All along, he’s still been the artist who got a job at The Odeon so that he could meet his heroes. He’s still painting away in his brownstone, doodling on notepads during concept meetings. He’s had shows recently at galleries such as Tiwa Select; he’s loosely associated with the Galerie Sardine extended universe; and he’s someone whose work I’ve been told about for years by those in the know.

As they put it, Tarlow is an emerging artist who happens to own the best all-around restaurant in Manhattan, as well as a bunch of other successful spots in Brooklyn.

“I realized, opening Borgo, that I really loved working in restaurants—and not that I had forgotten, but I hadn’t actually worked services in a while until I opened,” Tarlow told me during a studio visit. “And then, in a similar way, I think—I love making paintings. I actually will paint forever, no matter what happens.”

The studio had dozens of unstretched canvases heaped on the ground, some still rolled up, and others hanging via a pin on the studio wall. They showed figures grappling with pain in fierce color-blocked fields, automatic-painting abstractions, faces fading into other faces. One painting was a portrait of the artist Joe Bradley, a friend.

The studio is in the basement of the Fort Greene brownstone where Tarlow has lived for two decades with his wife, Kate Huling, raising four kids in a kind of neo-boho paradise. There were no studio assistants, no art handlers, no frames, no boxes, no packaging—just the artist and the work.

“It was kind of just as chaotic as everything else there, but in the most perfect warm embrace of a way. I saw the pure energy that he put into his paintings and the stories that they told,” says Alex Tieghi-Walker, the founder of Tiwa Select, calling from London. “So many artists could be quite—rightfully so, but quite precious with their works. And I love that Andrew was just like, ‘Oh, pull out the ones you’re taking and just take them in an Uber home.’”

Tarlow grabbed at a canvas bare-handed, one with a bit of a conceptual bent, and put it up on an easel.

“I’ve had this up on the wall for a while now, and I just continued to look at it because I’m happy with it. I’m also a little unsettled—I mean, I’m showing you the inside of my drawers. I’m also a little unsettled by how far it’s gone abstract-wise.”

He told me he couldn’t really do his other job, the restaurant job, without painting at odd hours. They’re totally separate, but complementary in a cosmic way.

“What are the processes? Like you said, for some people, it’s nine to five. Then you listen to the news, smoke a cigarette, drink coffee. It’s either working or it’s not. The door either opens or it’s not,” Tarlow said, gesturing around to his studio. “But I’m going to go here every day, and I’m going to push some paint on canvas.”

Diner opened in 1999, a few years after Tarlow moved to the desolate southern tip of Broadway in Williamsburg—where the crumbling street dead-ends into the East River. While looking for a cheap studio space, he found a 6,000-square-foot loft across the street from an abandoned diner from the 1920s. The loft’s landlord bought the diner, and in 1999, Tarlow opened Diner with then partner Mark Firth—and watched as it was patronized by only the artists across the street.

“You could stand outside the restaurant in those days and not see a single person walk by,” he told Bon Appetit in 2010.

Tarlow kept expanding. He opened Marlow & Sons, and then the butcher shop and specialty food store Marlow & Daughters. He founded a bakery, She Wolf, and a literary magazine, Diner Journal. He operated the restaurant at the Wythe Hotel, but only for a few years. Instead of doing the easy thing, Vegas-ifying Diner in some new development on the Williamsburg waterfront, he got even weirder, opening a nautical bar called Achilles Heel in a far-out corner of Greenpoint.

A dealer with a gallery in Tribeca was the first, but far from the last, to tell me I had to check out Tarlow’s paintings. After an introduction was brokered, Tarlow invited me to lunch at Borgo this past summer. The restaurant has many fantastic pork-laden dishes, but we ate almost entirely vegetables, as well as one very elegant, simple piece of fish. A summer lunch. We fell into an easy patter, talking about exhibitions, other artists—but mostly his painting practice. He’d been working on Long Island, not on the East End but in the middle. He’d had a few shows. There was discussion of representation. He spoke about all this with an unpracticed earnestness and complete confidence. He sounded like a very prominent emerging artist, which, at 56, he is.

“I don’t know if it’s just age or time, or I was too much of a young person, or a young mind, but I’ve been more secure with my ability to hold all these things in the same time,” he told me back in the studio. “I can go work tonight in the restaurant and feel perfectly confident in that work, and I can show you this work and feel perfectly confident in this work. Whereas, I think, as a young person, I felt like, Am I fake?”

Sometimes it’s not the enfant terrible who breaks out—it’s the working parent, the person with a desk job, the successful entrepreneur who back-ends into revolutionary art making. Think William Carlos Williams writing “The Red Wheelbarrow” while working as a doctor in Rutherford, New Jersey. Or Ruth Asawa making art in her kitchen while raising six children in San Francisco. Or Jeff Koons working on Wall Street in order to earn money to make his sculptures. Having a demanding job actually granted them the freedom to be artists. Tarlow started drawing during restaurant concept meetings.

Sometimes Tarlow hangs his own paintings upstairs in his brownstone’s salon room, or at his house on Long Island, to see what they look like in the wild. The paintings have a confident thrust to them, with the colors bold-blocked in a way that reminds me of Albert Oehlen, drawing from Roman and Greek mythology in Twombly-esque riffs: visages multiplying and fading like a Kippenberger-ian pomo ride into the ether. Sure, any painter who’s spent time in Europe since the 1990s has wanted to be Martin Kippenberger. But Tarlow has an actual connection to him: Like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a lover of Italian food and good wine, and he made art to hang in restaurants. And like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a restaurant owner, balancing his studio practice with running Capri, a Venice, California, spot in which he invested after moving to Los Angeles in 1989. According to those present at the time, Kippenberger became a part-owner of the place because, as the artist put it, “You can’t get a decent Bolognese in Los Angeles.”

As a bartender at The Odeon, Tarlow maintained a working painting studio but found it hard to produce art. After opening Diner, he skipped painting sessions in favor of opening businesses and starting a family. Once that duality settled, he started drawing on the move, carrying sketchbooks and working through potential paintings. Eventually, once the kids got old enough, he built out a studio in a nook of his 19th-century basement.

“I really started painting back downstairs. Let’s just say, after dinner, it was 8 p.m. and they were watching Nemo. No one actually needs me, they’re totally happy. My wife’s up there, everyone’s laughing, giggling with little fish,” he said. “And I can just walk down here and do my thing. Having it in my house for sure is the only way I could do this amount of work, and for sure even get to this place. Because I do think you have to do a certain amount of work to get to this place unless you’re just a born prodigy. But when you think about the genius of Picasso or whomever, he made a million fucking paintings.”

Tarlow didn’t really show anyone his work for a long time.

“I met Andrew socially. I knew his restaurants way before I knew Andrew. And one day he was like, ‘Come and see my studio,’” Tieghi-Walker tells me. “It did not surprise me at all that he had an art studio in his basement and that these were the types of works he was creating.”

The show at Tiwa Select was on view right as Tarlow was getting ready to open Borgo. There was a certain amount of unconscious transference, Tarlow told me. For the Tiwa dinner, instead of creating name placards, the artist hand-sketched an artwork of each guest’s name on the paper tablecloth. Now, when a regular makes a reservation at Borgo, Tarlow will elegantly sketch out their name on the paper tablecloth.

The showcasing of his art at Borgo marks the first time Tarlow has put his own work on the premises of his own restaurant. Tarlow doesn’t exactly promote this. When I asked about it, he told me that only one of his own works was up at the moment, then changed the subject. Alex Levy, the media strategist and theater producer, has been a regular at Borgo since it opened. “Borgo is the grown-up Platonic ideal of what a restaurant can be,” he said. After several visits, Levy, who also collects a bit of contemporary art, noticed what was on the walls.

“I complimented one of the paintings, and Andrew said, ‘It’s by my daughter.’ And then he pointed to another one and said, ‘That’s by me,’” Levy says. “I had no idea that there’s this whole other part of him.”

Like Tarlow, Levy balances two seemingly divergent but strangely complementary careers—as a speechwriter on one hand, a Tony Award winner on the other—and Tarlow invited him to see his studio on Long Island. Levy bought a painting immediately. Seeing the studio, Levy says, helped him realize, to some extent, what the special sauce is behind a place like Borgo. It’s for incredibly confident, hyperproductive creative types, run by an artist who has complete faith in his ability to work.

And for Tarlow, the focus and passion in one arena lead right into the passion for the other.

“I’m also being very present for your needs in the same way as I’m trying to be very present with these paintings,” he said. “They’re not separate boats. When the restaurant’s working, I feel creative inside of it.”

#3529. Witcher 4 Has Fewer People Working On It Than It Did 3 Months Ago, But Just Barely

As part of CD Projekt's latest earnings report, the Polish developer revealed new information about its projects and headcount.

For the quarter that ended on October 31, The Witcher 4 was the company's biggest project by headcount, with 513 people working on it. That's down from 519 people for the quarter that ended on July 31.

For comparison, the number of developers on Cyberpunk 2 rose from 184 to 199 and staffers on the new IP codenamed Hadar jumped from 33 to 34. The codename Sirius game, believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher game, saw its development staff shrink from 84 to 60; the project has undergone numerous shifts throughout its development as CD Projekt reworks the experience.

CD Projekt's total development headcount rose from 1,045 to 1,051.

In terms of money, CD Projekt reported Q3 revenue of 208 million PLN ($51 million USD) and net earnings of 109 million PLN ($26.8 million). CD Projekt spent a lot--more than 177 million PLN ($43.5 million) on development costs during the quarter--but the company's total cash reserves grew by 31 million PLN ($7.6 million USD).

CD Projekt has a number of big projects in the works, including The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past in 2027 and The Witcher 4 in 2028. Cyberpunk 2 is also on the way, but it doesn't have a release window yet. The company is also working on a game with Scopely, the mobile gaming giant owned by Saudi Arabia.

Cyberpunk 2 was in the news recently, as the game's creative director joked that the RPG is now canceled because GTA 6 is so good.

There have long been tall-tales about secret, forbidden video games in the grips of supernatural forces. Most of them, your Petscops, your Drowned BENs, are just a bit of online campfire scaries. But if one eccentric Japanese monk is to be believed, an obscure PlayStation disc from the â90s was a vessel for forbidden information. UFOlogist Takano Josen claims he managed to slip secret classified NASA documents into a commercially released video game. The problem is he canât remember which one.

Currently a practicing Buddhist monk, Josen spent most of his life meditating on unearthly obsessions. Heâs worked on TV programs and founded the ‘UFO Lovers’ party, which ran on a platform of building formal infrastructure for space aliens to land on. His biggest claim to fame is opening Cosmo Isle Hakui, a saucer-shaped emporium of space travel memorabilia and martian curios in Ishikawa prefecture.

A new YouTube video from American Alchemy host and Peter Thiel understudy Jesse Michels (warning, obscene amounts of AI therein) sits down with Josen. The interviewee claims to have embedded himself not just with other key believers but figures central to the American space program. In one of his wildest stories, Josen says he managed to persuade his way into NASAâs Houston base, created copies of classified UFO documents, and smuggled them on to a commercially released PlayStation game.

Josen says that in the mid-90s he worked on a UFO TV special, co-produced by Zombie Nation and Heiankyo Alien makers Meldac. The pitch was that alongside the program, viewers were told they could seek the PlayStation tie-in disc out for additional, authentic evidence. “Itâs not particularly impressive footage,” says Josen. “Lots of firefly-objects flying around.”

When Michels asks Josen what the name of the game is, he admits he doesnât recall. The YouTuber, and other UFO fans, do seem to have something dead to rights. Released in 1996, Yaoi Junichi Gokuhi Project UFO Wotsuie!! (or Top Secret Project Chase the UFO!!) is an interactive collection of alien footage hosted by Junichi Yaoi, a late night TV host and illustrious media figure. It wasnât made by Meldac, instead Chase the UFO was created by Umihara Kawase devs Clary Business. While itâs odd for Josen to cite such a specific, alternative publisher, it otherwise closely matches his description.

While much similar to multimedia suites weâre more accustomed to on personal computers, most of Japanâs PC-like games were developed for disc-based consoles like PlayStation and the Saturn due to a stronger player base. Yaoi produced a number of UFO TV specials, which the game launches itself off of. Chase the UFOâs collection is international and expansive, 1,100 photos and videos according to recent decompiles, but compressed to fit on the PlayStationâs own little saucer. More importantly, most of these resemble the type of media shared widely on all manner of â90s TV programs. Art Bell and The X-Files kicked off a cultural phenomenon that spawned all kinds of schlocky ‘exposes,’ such as Foxâs infamous Alien Autopsy. On PlayStation, you could parse through as full motion video Yaoi sits pensively at his computer.

The biggest glaring hole in Josenâs story isnât publisher particulars or dubious content creators, but just the yarn that he could sweet talk his way into the Johnson Space Center’s secret vaults and squirrel away classified files unnoticed. The ’90s were transfixed on aliens and government facilities, but into the 2000s and post-9/11 a lot of conspiracy culture re-aimed their sights on fellow terrestrials. What was once the center of the cultural universe is now in another galaxy. Over the last decade, Washington itself has produced what it claims to be footage of UFOs encountered by military personnel, but to dimmed enthusiasm and the subtext of drumming up defense budgets over seeking out cosmic neighbors.

I’ve written a lot about You Can See Everything, the hit documentary about Elizabeth Holmes that surprised everyone on the 2026 movie schedule. I’ve even written about a few spoilers, but now that the movie is available to buy on streaming, I’m here to ask you what the directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, asked us all to do months ago: keep the secrets secret! I admit it’s a little hypocritical to say that now, as I’ve spoiled the big secret in previous articles, but if you’re watching the movie with friends or loved ones on this Thanksgiving weekend and they don’t know about the spoilers, listen to the directors!

Right before the A24 film was released in September, Fielder and Oppenheim showed the movie at the New York Film Festival, and in a Q&A after the movie, Fielder talked about how the movie came to be. He said that they didn’t really know where it was going to take them, or how it would end. They especially didn’t foresee the second half of the movie, and in a way, it was as much of a surprise to them as it is to audiences.

I was spoiled on the movie that seemingly everyone is talking about, from former employees of Holmes to psychologists who've seen it, before I saw it, but the two people I saw it with were not, and honestly, it was so much fun to see and hear their reactions. Fielder wants that for everyone, and he made a plea to those in attendance at the screening to keep the movie’s secrets, as hard as it might be in this social media age. Fielder said to the audience:

The experience you guys had of, like, discovering it happening as it's happening, like we did. We really want audiences to have that experience when it opens, if possible, if you guys can preserve that in a way. I know some of you are probably going to be writing about this or whatever, but if we can preserve where we go in that section. I just love that everyone is having the experience you guys did.

Of course, it’s been a few months since the film was released and became one of the biggest box office hits of the year (and hit new milestones for documentaries), so many have either seen it or have had the big reveal spoiled, but I do think the reveal is critical to the message of the movie.

This won’t be the last time I write about this movie, as we still have the streaming release where it'll be available with an HBO Max subscription, likely sometime in January, and You Can See Everything will undoubtedly be up for a plethora of awards over the winter. So I’ll be busy writing about it, and honestly, likely talking about the reveal, but I promise I’ll always do so with a bold spoiler warning, just as I did when the movie first came out. We should all do the same!
